title: Procedural wood material with growth rings
purpose: Build a node-based wood material whose growth rings, latewood share, warp, pores, roughness and bump are parameters, and assign it to the active mesh. Use it for furniture, floors and props without image textures.

parameters.name: rings_per_metre
parameters.description: Growth rings per metre of radius from the object's Z axis.

parameters.name: latewood_fraction
parameters.description: Share of each ring taken by the dark latewood band.

parameters.name: warp
parameters.description: How far noise displaces the rings.

parameters.name: warp_scale
parameters.description: Frequency of the warping noise across the grain.

parameters.name: grain_stretch
parameters.description: How much longer noise features are along the grain (Z) than across it.

parameters.name: earlywood_color
parameters.description: Colour of the light earlywood band.

parameters.name: latewood_color
parameters.description: Colour of the dark latewood band.

parameters.name: pore_strength
parameters.description: How much the stretched pore noise darkens the colour.

parameters.name: roughness
parameters.description: Roughness in latewood and in earlywood (third value unused).

parameters.name: assign
parameters.description: Assign the material to the active mesh object.

outputs.description: One material with a node tree; assigned to the active mesh.

limits: Rings are cylinders around the object's local Z axis, so the grain follows the object's Z; rotate the object or edit the Grain Space mapping for other directions. Colours are a stylized approximation, not measured wood data. Pores come from stretched noise, not cell structure. Object coordinates make the pattern scale with the object. Rendered here with Cycles CPU only; EEVEE output is expected to match but was not rendered. Verified in Blender 5.2.1; written for the 4.2 API.
technique_references: Growth rings as fract(k * radial distance) from math nodes
Domain warping of coordinates by centred noise
Anisotropic noise by scaling the grain axis before sampling
